abril-fatface-inter: Inter reads like smooth tubing, its big counters letting light in. Abril Fatface swings between fat stems and razor-fine joins, giving the heading drama while the body keeps one constant nib width underneath.
anton-work-sans: Work Sans keeps its c tips well apart and its mean line high, giving text a modern, open texture. Anton crowds and commands; Work Sans lets each letter breathe.
archivo-cabin: Wide exits, tall letters: Archivo lets light straight through its large x-height forms. Cabin follows with bent-tubing letterforms, round bowls of uniform wall and friendlier open terminals at a moderate lowercase height.
azonix-technor: Azonix is wide-mouthed and commanding, with capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Azonix stays crisp when shrunk; Technor glows like neon tube, one line thickness with a wide channel into every bowl.
bebas-neue-work-sans: Bebas Neue packs a thick band of clustered letters with trimmed-looking ascenders and no stroke contrast at all. And the standout quality is that crowded-versus-open tension, since Work Sans keeps its c tips apart.
blade-runner-switzer: Cinematic hairlines nearly vanish beside the stems in Blade Runner Movie Font, whose terminals almost kiss the bowl. And Switzer, tubular and tall in the waist, stays open and approachable line after line.
boska-ibm-plex-sans: IBM Plex Sans opens a wide channel into every bowl, with a technical but approachable manner. But Boska does drama best, with stems like carved stone against paper-thin cross strokes.
boska-satoshi: Boska brings carved-stone stems and a bold a crowned with a hairline curve, bookish and dramatic. And Satoshi's soaring x-height and open e should keep paragraphs flowing easily, every stroke cut uniformly.
cabinet-grotesk-erode: Striking curves that never thin out at the turns, like neon sign tubing, make Cabinet Grotesk hard to ignore. Erode then reads with a gentle ebb and flow of weight.
cabinet-grotesk-satoshi: Satoshi has a soaring x-height and a wide-open e. Cabinet Grotesk, with a moderate lowercase and curves that never thin, still holds up if the heading is made small (say, in a real estate agent logo).
caveat-satoshi: Human and handwritten, Caveat clamps its letters tight, like a quick jot for a field notes page. But Satoshi, a sans-serif with a soaring x-height, stands much taller on the line and keeps every stroke uniform.
crimson-pro-ibm-plex-sans: Graceful, close-set letters with a gentle stroke shift. Crimson Pro is best at its smooth, modest gradient and clear round forms, while IBM Plex Sans does its best work with a wide channel into every bowl.
curated-alex-brush-gf-overpass-mono: Quiet calligraphy, code-style order: Alex Brush shades its curves gently (a boutique hotel logo, say) while Overpass Mono spaces fixed-width letters widely. Monospace text marches on, pleasant for a little while before the sameness builds.
curated-alfa-slab-one-gf-ancizar-sans: Ancizar Sans reads squeezed and modern, like typewriter keys. The real draw is raw weight: Alfa Slab One lands heavy and widely tracked, over compact text best kept to a line or two.
curated-alfa-slab-one-gf-im-fell-dw-pica: Alfa Slab One hits heavy and dense, its tracked curves coiling nearly shut. IM Fell DW Pica jostles its refined, literary letters together, and that clash of weight against finesse is the appeal for a couple of lines.
curated-alfa-slab-one-gf-pt-sans-narrow: Curves that coil nearly closed give Alfa Slab One a dense, heavy punch (think phone case art). PT Sans Narrow does the opposite job, tight-kerned and constant in stroke, for a modest bit of reading.
curated-alfa-slab-one-gf-story-script: Story Script is modern and clean, each word packed solid. Under Alfa Slab One's heavy, widely tracked slabs, that flat stencil-like line feels light, and it does its best with only a few words.
curated-alfa-slab-one-gf-voltaire: Alfa Slab One is heavy and dense, the kind of thing you'd see on a skate brand tee. Voltaire is snug, with one constant nib width, so over many lines it grows tiring and prefers a few words.
curated-alfa-slab-one-gf-yrsa: Dense and heavy, Alfa Slab One tracks generously, its curves coiling nearly shut. Yrsa hugs its letters close with a lightly shaded, dignified texture, though not built for pages of it.
curated-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-ca: Noto Sans Carian keeps open terminals like scissor blades, beside ornate Almendra Display (a vampire film title, say). Noto Sans Carian stays quiet while the heading flaunts a literary air and a pronounced x-height.
curated-almendra-display-gf-yaldevi: Ornate and literary, Almendra Display sweeps in with a tall x-height. Yaldevi answers in a plain sans, its oversized lowercase and open e making the sharpest difference from that decorated heading.
curated-amatic-sc-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab reads as a grounded classic serif, every lowercase letter standing tall and refined. And Amatic SC, with its quirky squeezed-toothpaste line, gives it a casual handwritten neighbor that suits something like a vape label.
curated-archivo-black-gf-markazi-text: Authoritative and urban, Archivo Black fills the line with weight. Where it hits hard and loud with generous room around each letter, Markazi Text, a classic serif, works quietly in a tight, bookish texture with soft stroke changes.
curated-archivo-black-gf-noto-serif-gran: Heavy, loud, unmistakably urban: that's Archivo Black. Noto Serif Grantha, a text serif with tempered contrast like a half-turned flat brush, would carry a longer read gently, its small letters looking pleasantly oversized.
curated-audiowide-gf-noto-sans-carian: Noto Sans Carian reads cleanly, its open terminals and small gaps below the ascenders keeping things crisp. Audiowide sits above it like futuristic tiles with wide grout lines, pencil-thin and uniform, so the sans-serif text feels grounded beneath it.
curated-bangers-gf-fira-code: Fira Code reads precise and technical, with open channels running between its letters. Fira Code's steady, minimal step from capitals to lowercase would suit a longer passage less well than brief copy, while Bangers supplies the loud tubing-like heading.
curated-bangers-gf-quando: Quando reads bookish, with sparse spacing and a big tall middle zone. A larger size for this classic serif may help, since it isn't meant for long paragraphs, and Bangers can shout above it (say, on a recipe zine).
curated-bangers-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab brings structure, its open-throated middle zone dominating each line. Bangers is the loud one, all commanding fun with no stroke contrast, while the slab-serif body does the precise, sturdy work for brief copy.
curated-bebas-neue-fs-azeret-mono: Commanding and editorial, Bebas Neue packs a thick band of tight, clustered capitals. It makes the statement, while Azeret Mono, a monospace with open mouths and generous spacing, does the quiet, precise work of text.
curated-bebas-neue-gf-platypi: Platypi reads bookish and literary, its curves swelling just slightly heavier than its joins. And Bebas Neue, flat and commanding with no stroke contrast, makes a striking counterweight (think a sci-fi movie title) to that soft text serif.
curated-bebas-neue-gf-vollkorn: Bebas Neue stacks its rod-like capitals into a tight, thick band, ideal for a class reunion poster, say. Vollkorn follows as a text serif with a faintly modulated line, comfortable until the heading shrinks and loses its punch.
curated-bebas-neue-libre-baskerville: Libre Baskerville stretches sideways with a bookish, refined stance and only a restrained shift between stem and joining stroke, set against tall, tightly clustered capitals. Its lowercase sits moderate and calm.
curated-berkshire-swash-gf-noto-sans-egy: Berkshire Swash is ornate but quiet, with bold downstrokes and ghostly upstrokes.  Noto Sans Egyptian Hieroglyphs answers with open, approachable letters and towering capitals, though it is not built for paragraph after paragraph.
curated-boska-gf-abel: Abel runs close-set like beads on a thread, every stroke bent from the same tubing. Boska brings the drama with a broad-nib pen's fat downstrokes and threadlike upstrokes, so a long page would feel steady and unfussy beneath it.
curated-boska-gf-barlow-condensed: Dramatic and bookish, Boska has razor-thin serifs on dense black pillars. Barlow Condensed packs its monotone letters like matchsticks, so the heading carries the mood while the body simply carries the words.
curated-boska-gf-beiruti: Boska cuts steep thick-thin strokes, handy for a jewelry brand logo, perhaps. Beiruti keeps a monoline skeleton with wide entrances into each letter, so extended text would flow quickly and without any fuss.
curated-boska-gf-economica: Dramatic Boska, with its thick-and-thin rhythm, could front a true crime podcast cover. Economica packs tubelike, constant-weight letters tightly together, which suits quick reading while the heading handles the theatrics.
curated-boska-gf-finlandica: Finlandica traces a constant-width outline you could follow with a finger, with open-mouthed e crossbars. Boska's sturdy verticals and feathery horizontals sit above it, giving a page a bookish crown and a modern, clean floor.
curated-boska-gf-harmattan: Harmattan draws contrast-free strokes with tight spacing and wide, barely curled s curves. Boska's hairlines nearly vanish beside its stems, so if the heading goes small, those fine strokes get lost.
curated-boska-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight bends its lines like rope, with short ascenders, for a home inspection report, say. Boska delivers heavy stems and hairline thins for drama, while the body keeps every stroke visible.
curated-boska-gf-madimi-one: Stone-heavy stems, scratch-fine serifs. Boska leans on ink-heavy verticals and thread-like diagonals, while Madimi One, a plain sans with nearly shut e and c, is happiest across a few lines.
curated-boska-gf-momo-trust-sans: Momo Trust Sans draws like a plotter pen, one line throughout. Boska's hairlines against massive stems add the drama, and paragraphs in the plain sans would flow smoothly, say, on a gallery website homepage.
curated-boska-gf-mona-sans: Dramatic is Boska's mood, with hairline crossbars perched on heavy verticals. Mona Sans, a sans-serif with openings like a door left ajar, is the welcome mat to that drama (a personal blog, say).
curated-boska-gf-nobile: Fat stems, wiry arms, pure drama. Boska does the showy work, while Nobile, a plain sans with open mouths like an unjoined chalk arc, handles the steady reading, say, in an email newsletter.
curated-boska-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian stands tall, with c, s and z full and generous. Against Boska's moderate lowercase, this sans-serif rises higher, an approachable counterweight to a dramatic, bookish serif.
curated-boska-gf-noto-sans-elbasan: Stout stems, razor hairlines, all theatrical. Size Noto Sans Elbasan a notch smaller than Boska; the plain sans has large lowercase and terminals that never pinch.
curated-boska-gf-paytone-one: Dramatic stuff: thick stems that dwarf the thin strokes beside them. Paytone One, a clean sans with chisel-groove narrowness, is better for a line or two of text, so give it a larger size.
curated-boska-gf-red-hat-text: Loud contrast, then a quiet line. Boska swings between fat and hairline strokes, while Red Hat Text, a plain sans drawn like a technical pen, gives the eye a constant outline to follow.
curated-boska-gf-rethink-sans: Boska's hairlines hang against massive stems. Rethink Sans, a sans with generous openings and a stroke that never varies, is the steady counterpoint, and that tension is the real draw.
curated-boska-gf-roboto: Roboto keeps its round letters generously open. Next to Boska's thin crossbars and thick stems, this sans reads low-contrast and straightforward, and the two hold together well (an interior design moodboard, say).
curated-boska-gf-telex: Telex has curvy, loosely drawn letters that read friendly and unfussy, a fine partner for a jewelry brand logo, say. Boska's heavy stems and hairline serifs give the page its drama.
curated-boska-gf-vazirmatn: Dramatic and bookish, with heavy verticals and thread-thin diagonals. Vazirmatn follows in a sans-serif that stays approachable, its wide s never pinching, so paragraphs move along easily without any strain.
curated-boska-gf-winky-sans: Winky Sans keeps its capitals low and modern. Its lowercase stands tall against Boska's sharp swings from thick to hairline, so a longer passage feels gentle and quick to follow (a personal blog, maybe).
curated-boska-gf-wix-madefor-text: Boska brings very fine thins against very thick strokes, bookish and dramatic. Wix Madefor Text, a sans-serif with open terminals, steps in underneath and gives the page somewhere easy to rest.
curated-bubblegum-sans-gf-fira-mono: Chunky, bubbly letters cut with a single width, like laser-cut sheet. Fira Mono follows with tall, widely spaced monospace glyphs, structured and precise, comfortable when you only need a little at a time.
curated-bungee-gf-scada: Scada is a plain sans with an approachable manner, happy to sit quietly beneath a loud heading (a metal album cover, perhaps). Bungee draws bold, separated letters with a drafting-pen line, while Scada handles the actual reading.
curated-bungee-inline-gf-lxgw-wenkai-mon: Bungee Inline spaces its decorative, retro glyphs far apart, like beads strung along a cord. And LXGW WenKai Mono TC, a precise monospace with fixed-width terminals, keeps the text tidy, better for brief copy.
curated-cabinet-grotesk-gf-b612-mono: Curves that stay thick right through the turns give Cabinet Grotesk its striking, cord-like look. B612 Mono, a monospace with extended tracking and an open e, makes a long stretch feel structured, say, for an engineering blog.
curated-cabinet-grotesk-gf-inconsolata: Inconsolata is a monospace with fixed-width, code-style letters and a ring-like c, structured and technical. Cabinet Grotesk does the striking part with stems and curves that never thin, while Inconsolata does the steady work of text.
curated-cinzel-decorative-fs-nunito: Widely spaced capitals with a mild shimmer of swelling strokes set Cinzel Decorative apart, fine for a yoga studio logo, say. Nunito then adds round, approachable lowercase in a plain sans, giving the commanding heading a softer partner.
curated-cinzel-decorative-fs-supreme: Regal swagger, with a possible detour into graffiti style lettering. Cinzel Decorative ripples faintly across wide-set capitals while Supreme lays a heavy, dense strip of plain sans beneath, grounding it.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-alumni-sans: Cinzel Decorative spreads its capitals wide, with stencil-cut letters and bar widths that vary only mildly across each word. Over pages, Alumni Sans Pinstripe knits into tight, uniform texture.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-arimo: Arimo reads openly, with a tall mean line and generous gaps. Cinzel Decorative leads with widely spaced capitals and tame contrast, fit for a wizard school crest, while this sans lets text run on page after page without tiring.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-candal: Open capitals above, closed-up curves below. Cinzel Decorative does its best work in commanding, widely spaced capitals, while Candal, generously letterspaced with wide porthole counters, handles the quieter lowercase.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-funnel-sans: Funnel Sans keeps its stroke widths constant, stem to curve. What stands out most is the gentle modulation of Cinzel Decorative against that flat, unvarying line, one soft and one clean.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-geist: Cinzel Decorative has ink-trace strokes and a restrained thick-thin ratio. It earns its keep big and brief, say for property management, beside Geist, a sans with one stroke width and wide openings.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-golos-text: Golos Text reads big and friendly, its x-height filling the line. Beneath Cinzel Decorative's gently modulated capitals, this sans-serif keeps one stroke width and a wide-parted s, so paragraphs flow without snagging.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-league-goth: League Gothic is tall-waisted and cramped, built for quick bursts of text. Open, widely spaced capitals are where Cinzel Decorative thrives; tight, closed letters are League Gothic's territory.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-magra: Big-bodied lowercase makes every word feel sturdy and low in contrast. Magra is the workhorse for text, while Cinzel Decorative earns attention with widely spaced, commanding capitals.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-major-mono-: Major Mono Display reads like neon tubing, spaced wide on every side. Cinzel Decorative brings comfortable stroke variation and refined capitals, while the monospace body keeps constant-width strokes precise and technical.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-a: Refined and a bit regal, Cinzel Decorative spreads its capitals wide (a sports club crest would sit happily in them). Noto Sans Avestan then follows in a modern, clean sans with open curve tips and a tall x-height, so the text stays easy to take in.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-b: Noto Sans Bassa Vah reads with a big midsection that swallows the line's height, and its c gapes like a pair of pliers. Cinzel Decorative adds the worn-stamp shimmer of restrained thick-thin strokes, and that is the quality that makes the pairing memorable.

Cinzel Decorative has thin strokes about half the weight of its thick ones, spread across wide, stately capitals. Noto Sans Buhid sits beneath in a plain sans with generous gaps where curves meet stems, and that quiet gap-filled openness is the strongest thing about the pair.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-d: Widely spaced capitals give Cinzel Decorative a ceremonial air. Its heavy-to-light strokes step down softly and make headlines feel crafted, while Noto Sans Duployan, with a wide-mouthed a and oversized counters, does the plain work of carrying the text.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-n:
Cinzel Decorative brings stately, widely spaced capitals.

Noto Sans Newa gives them a sans-serif partner with a clearly open e and tall bowls, so the faint upstroke and downstroke difference up top settles into easy text below.

Cinzel Decorative sets its widely spaced capitals with diagonals a touch thinner than the verticals, as if gently pressed. And it earns its keep big and short, while Noto Sans Nushu takes over with towering lowercase.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-o: Stately capitals, friendly text. Cinzel Decorative leans its heavier verticals like a gently tilted nib, while Noto Sans Old Turkic, chunky and tall in the lowercase, makes the whole combination feel approachable.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-s: Noto Sans Samaritan brings approachable, hefty lowercase letters with plenty of daylight inside every curve (handy for, say, a museum audio guide cover). Cinzel Decorative's mellow stroke range sits above and lets it read comfortably across paragraphs.

Widely spaced capitals with a mild shimmer of weight give Cinzel Decorative its air of command, fit for a dungeon master screen. Noto Sans Syloti Nagri then keeps the lowercase short in ascenders and tall in x-height beneath it.

Noto Sans Syriac reads like blown glass, its tall bowls and easy s turns feeling approachable. Cinzel Decorative earns its keep big and short, say, on a tattoo flash sheet, where its thin strokes sit not far from the thick ones.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-noto-sans-t: Widely spaced capitals give Cinzel Decorative a commanding, refined stance. It handles display drama, say a food truck logo, while Noto Sans Tai Viet handles the plain talking with its tall x-height and short ascenders.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-ramabhadra: Ramabhadra keeps a prominent x-height and a clean face. Cinzel Decorative does the showpiece work, with widely spaced capitals and a faint shimmer of weight changes, while the sans simply gets on with the reading.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-ruda: Cinzel Decorative sets its capitals far apart, with a faint shimmer of weight. Ruda's sizable x-height and wire-thin monoline strokes carry paragraphs along smoothly, with a monogram lettering as one passing possibility up top.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-truculenta: Truculenta reads compact and upright, its rounds still open to the side. Beneath the widely spaced capitals of Cinzel Decorative, paragraphs of this plain sans move briskly, its w drawn without thick or thin strokes.
curated-cinzel-decorative-gf-yaldevi: Refined from the first capital, Cinzel Decorative sits wide and slightly shimmering, with rounded letters that thicken at their sides. Yaldevi simply speaks plainly, its e open to the right.
curated-cinzel-decorative-montserrat: Stately, widely spaced capitals: Cinzel Decorative adds a faint swell to every curve. Montserrat gives long text oversized e and a counters, a sans-serif line that glides under the eye like wire.
curated-cinzel-decorative-mulish: Stately and shimmering, Cinzel Decorative stands wide and tall-bodied. What stands out is how Mulish's wire-like monoline strokes and horseshoe-open apertures quiet the faint weight shifts inside the heading's letters.
curated-clash-display-gf-alegreya-sans: Crisp, striking Clash Display could front a little league banner. Alegreya Sans, with broad g and a apertures and tight letterfit, handles a few lines nicely, so give Clash Display the bigger size.
curated-clash-display-gf-b612: Clash Display is striking and precise, ready for a golf tournament signage job. B612 is approachable and contemporary, but across long paragraphs its plain build would tire, so it prefers a few sentences.
curated-clash-display-gf-caladea: Crisp and striking up top, Clash Display stays plain. Caladea brings a restful line, thin points that keep real weight, and modest swings, good for brief notes, so make the heading the larger size.
curated-clash-display-gf-charis-sil: Charis SIL reads dignified and bookish, with curves that thin out modestly. Clash Display is the sharp, precise voice for a big opening line, while the body carries a quick bit of reading.
curated-clash-display-gf-ledger: Striking, then bookish: Clash Display over Ledger, maybe on a photographer signature mark. If Clash Display goes small, its striking edge fades, and if Ledger grows large, its pen-steady shading no longer feels like an easy quick read.
curated-clash-display-gf-maname: Maname brings a bookish, editorial feel, as on, say, a boutique hotel logo. Clash Display is best at striking, precise headlines, and Maname is best at carrying a few lines with sturdy hairlines.
curated-clash-display-gf-mohave: Mohave reads professional and approachable, with tight spacing throughout. What lifts the pair is Clash Display's striking precision against Mohave's wire-thick strokes, fine for a few lines or, say, a surf shop logo.
curated-clash-display-gf-proza-libre: Clash Display stands up front, striking and precise. Its best trick is how Proza Libre's approachable, modern sans body lets that sharp heading keep the spotlight across a few lines.
curated-cormorant-gf-noto-sans-sora-somp: Graceful and bookish, Cormorant leads. Its heavy strokes nearly vanish where they turn, while Noto Sans Sora Sompeng offers spacious, modern clarity for a few lines, even on a podcast cover art mock-up.
curated-covered-by-your-grace-fs-neco: Neco is a dignified, authoritative serif. Covered By Your Grace scribbles friendly and closed up front, while Neco's open, never-pinching curves let a few lines flow with a measured swell.
curated-creepster-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Pilcrow Rounded reads warm and open, its curves refusing to close. Creepster supplies the spooky shout for, say, a creepy carnival poster, while Pilcrow Rounded wants a generous size for a quick read.
curated-dafont-a-damn-mess-fs-rowan: A Damn Mess hollers raw, unpolished lines, as on a marching band banner. Rowan, by contrast, is the friendly serif that handles a quick read, its curves open where the heading's monoline stays blunt.
curated-dafont-aaargh-crimson-pro: Strong and tubular, Aaargh hits like bent copper pipe. Crimson Pro is the refined counterweight, with gently modulated strokes and no sharp hairlines that make long paragraphs feel settled.
curated-dafont-aaargh-fs-chillax: Relaxed spaghetti-loose Chillax letters lounge beneath Aaargh, whose stout, commanding shapes make a plain sans body feel easygoing (lockout and locksmith, maybe). Aaargh earns its keep big and brief.
curated-dafont-aaargh-fs-gambetta: Aaargh draws every stroke as stout as a pipe cleaner, while Gambetta's text serif lets its weight shift gently through wide channels into each counter. Long paragraphs would read bookish and graceful.
curated-dafont-aaargh-fs-tabular: Aaargh hits hard, with stout strokes and a wide-open e. Tabular's fixed-width monospace letters, each spaced clear of the next (say, for an embedded firmware console), make the sharpest foil: shouting up top, ticking along below.
curated-dafont-abberancy-fs-epilogue: Epilogue brings curvy, approachable letters with stubby ascender tips and a wire-like skeleton, set against the pinched, rebellious shapes of Abberancy. Tight closed heading forms against open body ones is the strongest quality here.
curated-dafont-adam-fs-sentient: Sentient reads with pinched apertures and crossbars a touch thinner than its stems, a sophisticated serif voice with subtle pen-like swells. And Adam does its best work with open, round letters and diagonals as hefty as its stems.
curated-dafont-adrenaline-fs-rowan: Cramped, shoulder-hugging letters with nearly enclosed counters give Adrenaline its punch (say, an art fair booth banner). Rowan's classic serif opens every curve wide, though it wasn't meant for long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-adrenaline-fs-spline-sans: Dynamic and tightly packed, Adrenaline crowds its round letters shut above a body with wide gaps between curve ends and stems. Spline Sans keeps every stroke at identical weight, which suits small doses.
curated-dafont-ahellya-fs-sentient: Razor-thin arcs against weighty stems, cut like a chisel notch in wood, mark Ahellya as delicate and understated (say, a boutique shop sign). Sentient's serif has pinched apertures and a modest weight gap, good for a handful of lines.
curated-dafont-ahellya-sora: Sora keeps its curves precise and geometric, never swelling at the turns. Ahellya's hairline joins and heavy blunt stems carry the flowing pen-written feel, while Sora does the quiet work of staying crisp and open.
curated-dafont-akira-expanded-fs-asap: Wide, loud, unmistakable. Akira Expanded stands like pins in a board, and Asap, a plain sans with a body height nearly matching its capitals, can stay modest in size without losing its footing.
curated-dafont-akira-expanded-fs-gambett: Graceful and bookish, Gambetta takes the quiet role. Beneath Akira Expanded's wide display, this classic serif, maybe for an accounting firm wordmark, can go a touch larger so its shifting strokes show.
curated-dafont-akira-expanded-gf-oxygen-: Oxygen Mono lays out fixed-width, code-style characters at a comfortable arm's length, say, for an esports team jersey. And Akira Expanded stretches above it like pins in a wide board, so that body text feels structured and unhurried.
curated-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-fira-: Fira Sans draws its curves wide open with diagonals as heavy as its verticals, and a larger-than-usual x-height. Under Alien Encounters, it keeps paragraphs steady and easy going.
curated-dafont-alien-encounters-fs-karma: Alien Encounters goes otherworldly, with big gaps between letter pairs (a fantasy campaign map might love it). Its heading is built to startle, whereas Karma, a trustworthy serif with gentle modulation, is built to keep the eye moving smoothly.
curated-dafont-alien-encounters-gf-fira-: Fira Mono spaces its glyphs far apart, tall and structured, say, for a tabletop rpg book. Alien Encounters leaves big gaps of its own, so the heading and monospace body feel like one spacious, technical system.
curated-dafont-amadeus-fs-alpino: Alpino reads cozy and casual, tall in the body with tightly spaced lines. Amadeus stretches wide with a pressure-free ballpoint line, and that wide-versus-snug difference is what makes the pair memorable.
curated-dafont-angeline-vintage-fs-synon: Synonym draws open, dependable curves in a constant stroke. Angeline Vintage hugs its letters close and romantic above, so the sans below lets the script breathe, though neither is meant for long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-angeline-vintage-space-gr: Space Grotesk reads neutral and geometric, its open counters like a hollow reed cut open (say, on an art deco invitation). Make Angeline Vintage small and its hugging letters clot, so it wants the room.
curated-dafont-angst-fs-familjen-grotesk: Angst stands tall and pinched, its closed letters drawn with one fixed nib and no swell on any downstroke. Familjen Grotesk leaves its bowls open on one side and stays lively, best for a line or two.
curated-dafont-another-danger-gf-datatyp: Datatype reads like a typewriter, every letter the same width. Another Danger is commanding and plain above it, while the monospace body stays precise, not made for long paragraphs (a conference lanyard badge for devs, maybe).
curated-dafont-aquiline-two-outfit: Aquiline Two is a delicate, soft script with a short, packed lowercase (an eyewear brand might like it). And Outfit glides beneath on cable-smooth sans strokes, made for quick reading.
curated-dafont-arkhip-sora: Letters float well apart in Arkhip, every stroke unvarying and geometric. Sora, the sans below, turns its corners cleanly without any pressure swell and keeps its precise curves widely parted.
curated-dafont-aston-script-gf-red-hat-m: Red Hat Mono reads in measured beats, each fixed-width letter marching in lockstep with the next. And Aston Script adds a relaxed calligraphic hand, so casual warmth meets technical precision, though not for long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-aston-script-space-grotes: Relaxed and casual, Aston Script writes with a slight swell. Space Grotesk draws glyphs as ribbons of constant width, a firm counterweight to the loose hand, made for brief reading, say, a wedding monogram.
curated-dafont-azonix-fs-paquito: Paquito is confident and approachable, with caps barely above lowercase. Azonix is best at authority, its wide-mouthed letters staying crisp even when shrunk (a landscaping company logo, possibly), while Paquito handles the friendly reading.
curated-dafont-bebas-kai-fs-azeret-mono: Azeret Mono spaces its monospace letters expansively, with open mouths and a lowercase packed up close to the caps. Bebas Kai stays compact above, and both prefer only a few words.
curated-dafont-bebas-kai-fs-trench-slab: Trench Slab reads dignified, with caps barely taller than its lowercase. Bebas Kai stays compact and smooth, so give Trench Slab a bit more size and avoid long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-berylium-fs-ranade: Minimal and contemporary, Berylium keeps its letters at a polite distance. Where it excels is pen-plotter smoothness, while Ranade excels at an organic, slightly shifting weight you feel more than see.
curated-dafont-beyond-wonderland-gf-cops: Tight, enchanting letters, handy for a coffee roaster logo. Beyond Wonderland sits snug and low, Copse lets daylight into every curve, and neither is built for pages of dense text.
curated-dafont-biko-fs-chillax: Cozy, uniform strokes in Biko meet the spaghetti-like line of Chillax (think fairy tale book cover), and the two feel related. A full page would drift along casually, like a relaxed chat.
curated-dafont-birds-of-paradise-fs-tabu: Long ascenders and descenders tower over a tiny lowercase core in Birds of Paradise, squeezed like typewriter keys. Tabular then marches in with fixed-width, gapped characters, best kept to a brief stretch of text.
curated-dafont-bit-cell-fs-rowan: Rowan reads friendly and literary, fine for, say, a retro gas station tee. Bit Cell brings closed, digital shapes that sit tightly stacked beside the open curves of Rowan, a pairing made for brief bursts of text.
curated-dafont-blackpine-fs-plein: Casual and expressive, Blackpine writes in a rope-steady calligraphic hand. Plein opens a clear channel into each round letter, the sharpest foil to the closed script, though it wants modest bites rather than marathons.
curated-dafont-blackpine-zilla-slab: Blackpine writes casually, in one rope-like line with tight spacing. Zilla Slab adds sturdy, technical slab-serif footing with broad open bowls, giving the script something solid to lean on, though only for brief reading.
curated-dafont-blade-runner-movie-font-f: Familjen Grotesk reads lively, with bowls left open on one side, made for brief bursts (game achievement badges, say). And Blade Runner Movie Font earns its keep big and short, hairlines nearly vanishing beside the stems.
Hind reads steady and open, fine for, say, holographic hud text. Blade Runner Movie Font brings cinematic hairlines and closed shapes, so give Hind a modest size and keep it to brief runs of copy.
curated-dafont-blade-runner-movie-font-g: Noto Serif Vithkuqi brings editorial stems and big round bowls with soft thickness shifts (say, a gaming video thumbnail). Blade Runner Movie Font cuts in with razor joins, kept to quick lines.
curated-dafont-blessed-day-fs-spline-san: Approachable Blessed Day sits low and close (a rehearsal dinner invite, say). Spline Sans brings rounded, uniform strokes that read smoothly and contemporary, though pages of dense paragraphs would wear the pair thin.
curated-dafont-blessed-day-sora: Sora keeps its curves smooth and its c and s widely parted. Blessed Day's low, calligraphic lowercase sits tight and hairline-fine above it, graceful enough for, say, a memorial service invitation.
curated-dafont-blockletter-fs-merriweath: Blockletter draws everything with a pencil-thin outline and a squat, tall belly. Merriweather Sans answers in sturdy, large-looking lowercase with an e that opens clearly, so one is sketched and the other built for reading.
curated-dafont-blockletter-fs-paquito: Paquito's caps and lowercase sit nearly shoulder to shoulder in height. Blockletter's single flat line weight runs through every glyph, so the heading feels drawn while this text serif feels confident and settled.
curated-dafont-bloody-fs-public-sans: Big round lowercase bowls give Bloody its menace, fit for, say, a gothic novel cover. Public Sans follows with a hefty, trustworthy body, and a large heading over modest body text suits the two.
curated-dafont-borg-fs-rowan: Cosmic and commanding, Borg stacks its glyphs tight like cut sheets. And Rowan, a friendly text serif with generous curve openings, is good for a handful of lines beneath it.
curated-dafont-borg-gf-new-tegomin: Borg packs its glyphs together with moderate contrast, a bold fit for a tech startup wordmark. New Tegomin is a dignified text serif with a ring-like c, though not meant for long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-braxton-fs-gambetta: Graceful and relaxed, Braxton hides tiny gaps that vanish when it shrinks. Gambetta's wide channels into each counter open things up, so make that serif larger, say for a hotel bar menu.
curated-dafont-brownhill-script-fs-synon: Slender, personal, quietly luxurious. Brownhill Script thickens and thins in gentle steps while Synonym lays down a plain sans stripe of constant ink, so one flows and the other simply stands there steadily.
curated-dafont-brownhill-script-plus-jak: Plus Jakarta Sans bends like a steel rod, monoline and modern, with curve endings kept well apart. Brownhill Script's low, calligraphic lowercase and neat hairlines make the contrast between the two the pair's strongest quality.
curated-dafont-brusher-outfit: Outfit draws every curve like bent cable, finishing well before it closes. Shrink Brusher, though, and its cord-heavy curves and wide-open e lose their romance, so give the plain sans body the smaller job.
curated-dafont-bushcraft-fs-epilogue: Wiry, wide-spaced and artistic, Bushcraft hangs its capitals and lowercase at nearly the same height, say, on a photo book cover. Epilogue follows in a curvy, monoline sans whose tall lowercase would carry a long page without tiring.
curated-dafont-caffeen-fs-epilogue: Epilogue draws curvy, wire-thin letters with tall bodies. Caffeen's tight, nearly colliding glyphs and stems-matching-bars give the pair its strongest quality: a chunky headline over a loose, friendly text line.
curated-dafont-caffeen-gf-fauna-one: Approachable Caffeen crowds its towering lowercase together, its bars as heavy as its stems. Fauna One slips in underneath, literary and low-slung, like a quiet librarian.
curated-dafont-caffeen-gf-piazzolla: Caffeen's glyphs nearly collide, each bar as heavy as its stems. Piazzolla's refined serif, with lowercase close to capital height and a pried-open e, gives the pair its strength: dense up top, spacious below.
curated-dafont-caviar-dreams-fs-literata: Caviar Dreams keeps every stroke wire-thin, with small low counters and pointed ascenders. Literata adds a bookish thick-and-thin rhythm, so if the text needs adjusting, nudge its size rather than the heading's.
curated-dafont-cheri-fs-erode: Inviting and cute, Cheri writes in a calligraphic hand with no hairlines at all. Its strongest quality is the pull against Erode, a dignified serif whose strokes swell and ease, giving the pair a warm, editorial tension.
curated-dafont-cheri-fs-supreme: Cute and inviting, Cheri holds its line width through every turn of its calligraphic hand. Supreme's heavy, crisp sans, with letters held open, gives the pair its strongest quality: a playful script beside a sturdy, steady text.
curated-dafont-cheri-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab gives a yoga studio logo, say, a structured footing under Cheri's calligraphic script. If the heading shrinks, its thread-like curves can thin out, while the slab-serif keeps the page anchored.
curated-dafont-chinese-rocks-montserrat: Striking wire-cut capitals from Chinese Rocks crowd tight together with little height difference between cases. And Montserrat spreads out beneath, its oversized counters and gliding curves making a long read feel like open air.
curated-dafont-chunk-five-fs-literata: Chunk Five is industrial and tightly spaced, its bowls nearly sealed shut. It does blunt impact best, while Literata handles bookish, open-mouthed text, with a thick-and-thin rhythm that a text serif needs.
curated-dafont-chunk-five-fs-tabular: Impactful and industrial, Chunk Five packs its nearly sealed bowls tight. Tabular, a monospace with open, separated characters, turns stiff and mechanical quickly if asked to carry long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-cloister-black-fs-amulya: Ornate, solemn Cloister Black, say, on a Halloween candy label. Amulya's sans curves stay generous and modern, and nudging its size up makes brief stretches of text comfortable.
curated-dafont-conthrax-fs-asap: Geometric Conthrax has lowercase so tall the capitals barely rise above it. If the heading shrinks, Asap's readable sans-serif body, with its open arcs, starts to compete for attention.
curated-dafont-cowboys-fs-plein: Cowboys has rustic, authoritative letters with wide gaps between stems, say, for a cabin rental sign. Plein's reliable sans tidies up underneath, giving the wide-spaced heading a steady partner.
curated-dafont-cubic-gf-grandiflora-one: Grandiflora One brings a literary, authoritative voice with tall ascenders. Cubic above it flares its terminals with a marker-nib line, and the serif is best given only a couple of lines.
curated-dafont-cubic-sora: Cubic leads with a nostalgic, marker-nib line and tall capitals. Sora's precise sans-serif turns corners without pressure swell, a tidy foil for those flared terminals, and happiest with a few lines.
curated-dafont-diner-general-sans: Friendly Diner draws monoline letters (say, for alien language lettering). General Sans stands out for steady pen pressure from first letter to last, its lowercase filling the line.
curated-dafont-diner-gf-b612-mono: Friendly, nostalgic monoline Diner, say, for a hackathon project demo. B612 Mono, a monospace with extended spacing, feels structured and technical against Diner's friendly warmth, and suits only a few lines.
curated-dafont-diploma-fs-synonym: Diploma's curves wrap so far around they almost lock, with a soft modulation like hand-drawn ink. Synonym's constant stripe of ink is the steadiest part, comfortable in modest amounts.
curated-dafont-diploma-gf-google-sans-co: Curves that wrap round until they almost lock define Diploma, with a soft, hand-inked modulation. And Google Sans Code's unmodulated monospace beat lends a precise counterweight, too measured for long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-diploma-gf-habibi: Traditional curves in Diploma wrap round until they nearly lock shut. Habibi lets the eye slip gently into each round letter, built for brief reading, even a blackletter tattoo.
curated-dafont-dirty-headline-gf-suwanna: Suwannaphum brings dignified, high-set serif letters beneath Dirty Headline, handy for a western ranch brand. Suwannaphum keeps its open letters breathing while Dirty Headline crowds its closed ones tight.
curated-dafont-disorder-fs-paquito: Disorder has no swelling where curves meet stems, so it looks raw. It makes big, chaotic statements, while Paquito, confident and approachable with caps close to its lowercase height, does the talking.
curated-dafont-dited-fs-chillax: Dited sits its shapes hip to hip, digital and tech through and through. Chillax loosens it with spaghetti-like lines and unfinished loops, casual enough to enjoy a bit at a time.
curated-dafont-dogica-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab is precise and structured, fit for a backcountry ski brand. Its middle zone dominates each line, and the open throats keep paragraphs moving, while heavy, widely tracked Dogica stands above.
curated-dafont-electroharmonix-fs-asap: Asap reads quickly, with open arcs, handy for a d&d character sheet. Its body height nearly matches the capitals, so paragraphs flow smoothly beneath Electroharmonix, whose striking letters stand apart.
curated-dafont-espresso-dolce-manrope: Espresso Dolce writes in a calligraphic hand (think a company letterhead sheet). It handles decoration with understated glow, while Manrope, approachable and clean, keeps every curve open and the lowercase tall.
curated-dafont-ethnocentric-bitter: Bitter reads dependable and grounded, with big lowercase eyes and see-through s shapes. Ethnocentric, fast and aggressive, earns its keep big and short, pushing its letters apart while Bitter stays put.
curated-dafont-existence-fs-erode: Erode reads dignified, with a tall middle band and shallow ascenders. Existence, industrial and modern, brings hard-edged weight with no pinched joins, so give it generous size above Erode.
curated-dafont-feast-of-flesh-bb-fs-paqu: Squinting, stubby-pencil tall: Feast of Flesh BB looks extreme. The shout of that heading against confident, approachable Paquito is what lingers, best kept to a few words (a wizard school crest, say).
curated-dafont-feast-of-flesh-bb-gf-alme: Almendra is a bookish serif with a deep-bellied lowercase, say, for a tabletop rpg handout. And Feast of Flesh BB, towering and extreme, is best for a few loud lines while Almendra handles the rest.
curated-dafont-feast-of-flesh-bb-gf-noto: Noto Serif Kannada reads literary, with big counters in a tall lowercase. Feast of Flesh BB pushes towering marker-tip strokes against that gentle shading (on a medieval tavern menu, maybe), though neither is built for long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-fenwick-fs-hoover: Fenwick keeps every line the same width, with bowls that fill the line. Hoover brings low contrast and a generous e entry, so against Fenwick's zero-contrast line (think watch brand dial text) the step feels deliberate.
curated-dafont-fenwick-fs-karma: Karma, trustworthy and classic (a yacht charter brand, say), keeps its taper modest. Fenwick above gives diagonals and horizontals matching heft, and Karma below tapers modestly, like a sharpened carpenter's pencil line.
curated-dafont-fenwick-fs-nunito: Nunito is an approachable sans with big, round lowercase bowls. Fenwick does its best work as the graceful, literary serif up top, bowls un-thinned at the sides, while Nunito handles the contemporary, rounded text beneath.
curated-dafont-foglihten-lora: Lora reads literary and bookish, with a welcoming c, say, on mailer tape. Foglihten earns its keep large and short, where its heavy blunt stems and pen-cut hairlines show, while Lora keeps its contrast tempered for brief reading.
curated-dafont-foglihten-satoshi: Satoshi is a sans-serif with a soaring x-height and a wide-open e. Every stroke has uniform width, so lengthy text feels smooth and unshaded next to the dark stems and feathery joins of Foglihten.
curated-dafont-forza-fs-literata: Literata is a bookish serif with wide-mouthed curves and sturdy hairlines, handy for, say, a welding and fabrication project. Forza's crowded, closed letters sit tight against that open, swelling text.
curated-dafont-forza-fs-ranade: Tightly strung Forza, rod-stock stiff, with closed-in letters. Ranade lets its widely spaced, open strokes breathe with only a slight rubber-cord shift in weight, so the two feel like a clenched fist beside an open hand.
curated-dafont-forza-fs-sentient: Forza crowds marker-tip letters together like beads on a wire, best where precision counts. Sentient takes the quieter job, with pinched apertures and sturdy thin strokes, say in a parts catalog.
curated-dafont-franchise-fs-alpino: Franchise stands tall and narrow, its letters jammed shoulder to shoulder like bent tubing. Alpino is a cozy plain sans with a tall body, so give it a bit more size than usual, say for a little league banner.
curated-dafont-franchise-fs-erode: Franchise is all tall, tight, uniform strokes, while Erode brings a classic serif's soft swell and dignified editorial polish. Stiff and supple meet here.
curated-dafont-franchise-gf-victor-mono: Franchise runs tall and tightly packed, every stroke the same thickness from stem to curve. Victor Mono is a loose, precise monospace, its bowls left open on one side, and that looseness is the pair's best quality.
curated-dafont-galaxy-gf-fauna-one: Fauna One reads literary and dignified, with a low-slung serif body and a generous opening into each e. Galaxy is the louder one, dense and cosmic with unbroken strokes, while Fauna One handles the quiet detail, say, a safety notice poster.
curated-dafont-galette-fs-literata: Authoritative but understated, Galette trims its spacing thin and keeps horizontals as heavy as verticals. Literata, a bookish text serif, tapers just slightly beside it, say, on a perfume bottle label.
curated-dafont-gallow-tree-fs-amulya: Rustic and weathered, Gallow Tree varies its strokes only a little, with closed curves and slim exits. Amulya brings modern openness in its curves, and that gap between old-world heft and contemporary ease is the pair's real strength.
curated-dafont-ghastly-panic-author: Ghastly Panic draws every line as if traced with a single neon marker tip, jittery and nearly touching. And Author, a refined serif with a faint swell in each bowl, gives that frenzy somewhere dignified to settle.
curated-dafont-gobold-fs-bespoke-slab: Commanding and wide-set, Gobold spreads its curves that never quite close. Bespoke Slab grounds it with tall, refined serif bodies, a steady counterweight (handy for retrospective slides) to all that sprawl.
curated-dafont-gobold-fs-erode: Commanding and geometric, Gobold locks its stems and arcs together in lockstep. Erode adds a mild shimmer of weight changes in its serif text, so the page gets both muscle and a gentle pulse.
curated-dafont-grinched-fs-spline-sans: Grinched towers in tall capitals packed snug as tiles, dominating every line it sits on. Spline Sans responds with sans strokes of identical weight and wide, friendly gaps, loosening the mischief just enough.
curated-dafont-grinched-gf-laila: Towering capitals dominate every line of Grinched, packed together like tiles with thin grout between them. Laila, a serif, loosens things with generous curves, pleasant for a few paragraphs.
curated-dafont-groovy-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla, a text serif, could sit under alphabet flashcards without fuss. Groovy's blunt, marker-round letters and slit-like c lean friendly and funky, while Piazzolla's open e and capital-sized lowercase keep the text steady.
curated-dafont-gunplay-gf-red-hat-mono: Red Hat Mono reads measured and exact, like a ballpoint line. Gunplay's nearly closed geometric forms against the open monospace below create a sharp tension, best taken a screenful at a time.
curated-dafont-guttural-gf-glegoo: Wide-mouthed curves and big counters make this serif read generously, set against Guttural's brush-pressed forms folded nearly shut. Glegoo's tall lowercase keeps paragraph after paragraph feeling refined and editorial, never cramped.
curated-dafont-guttural-gf-holtwood-one-: Guttural's brush-pressed curves fold nearly shut, dense and commanding enough for a zombie walk poster. Yet Holtwood One SC, a wide-tracked text serif, is for punchy lines rather than long paragraphs.
curated-dafont-halogen-fs-gambetta: Sleek Halogen bends like a steel rod, free of hairlines. It earns its keep big and brief, while Gambetta, a graceful serif with gently shifting stroke weight, adds bookish warmth (a style guide would not mind).
curated-dafont-halogen-fs-merriweather-s: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy, its tall lowercase making words look large. Halogen does its best work with sleek, uniform strokes, diagonals matching the uprights in weight, while the body sans keeps its e open to the right.
curated-dafont-halogen-gf-geist-mono: Geist Mono is structured and technical, a monospace with high-rising lowercase. Halogen is strongest at sleek, bent-steel curves, while the code-style body does its best work giving each letter wide side gaps.
curated-dafont-hammerhead-gf-biorhyme-ex: Blunt, industrial outlines fit a pressure washing flyer nicely. Hammerhead's plain unmodulated outline is its strength, while BioRhyme Expanded, a refined serif, opens wide gaps that split each word into single letters.
curated-dafont-hammerhead-gf-fenix: Fenix reads classic and editorial, a text serif whose curved strokes stop before turning inward. And Hammerhead's plain, unmodulated outline, drawn like a pen that never changes pressure, lends the whole thing industrial authority.
curated-dafont-hammerhead-gf-solway: Industrial and blunt, Hammerhead draws a plain unmodulated outline up top, while Solway's text serif keeps its flat, stencil-like line weight below. Authority, plainly.
curated-dafont-hero-fs-ranade: Hero sweeps a long, slow line across widely spaced, closed letters. Ranade's sans-serif answers with open shapes and hairlines neither wispy nor heavy, a loose, organic neighbor that could suit an in-app notification.
curated-dafont-hiruko-fs-chillax: Precise and pencil-thin, Hiruko never thickens or thins a line, while Chillax loosens into curves that trail off like spaghetti. Both share a similar build, so a long page stays easygoing.
curated-dafont-hiruko-gf-alyamama: Alyamama sets a traditional, refined serif under Hiruko's pencil-like monoline sans-serif, its curve endings held well apart. Hiruko stays uniform and exact, Alyamama softens into a tempered thick-thin stroke that never goes razor-fine; that gap is the pair's whole appeal.
curated-dafont-impact-label-gf-graduate: Heavy beads on a rod, each letter standing alone. Impact Label hits hard with a high-set x-height, then Graduate follows in a bookish classic serif with generous spacing and bowls drawn at stem thickness.
curated-dafont-joystix-satoshi: Approachable and tall in the lowercase, Satoshi reads as a sans-serif with every stroke cut to one width. Joystix is the loud one, widely tracked arcade lettering with a slight tug of heavier verticals, ready for a esports team jersey if needed.
curated-dafont-junegull-fs-asap: Asap reads openly, its c forms arcs and its body height nearly matching the capitals. And Junegull, pinched and cast-iron sturdy with retro friendliness, does the showy work, maybe on a 70s band poster.
curated-dafont-junegull-gf-major-mono-di: Retro cast-iron charm meets neon glass. Junegull pinches its curves shut with no thick-thin flicker, while Major Mono Display's tube-like monospace strokes sweep open, so a longer passage would glow slowly and feel technical.
curated-dafont-kawaii-fs-tabular: Tabular lays down fixed-width, code-style monospace with clear gaps between every character. Kawaii pops back with tall stems over stubby ink-blot lowercase and tight counters, sweet against systematic (say, for an open source project logo).
curated-dafont-kawaii-gf-montaga: Sweet and stubby, Kawaii crowds its round letters tight beneath tall stems, with Montaga's editorial text serif trailing open, unfinished loops below. Give Montaga a bit more size than usual.
curated-dafont-kawaii-gf-sanchez: Kawaii is all pop, tall stems over stubby, ink-blot lowercase. Kawaii is best at grabbing attention in a line, while Sanchez, a serif with open, caliper-like c shapes, handles anything wordier.
curated-dafont-keshia-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a ruler-straight line of constant ink, with generous openings in every curve, beneath the gem-snug letters of Keshia. Keshia's mild thicks and Synonym's flat line make a quiet, brief pairing.
curated-dafont-keshia-gf-google-sans-cod: Keshia sets snug, gem-cut script with a near-circular c. Google Sans Code, a monospace, spaces each word into a measured, wire-round beat, so a few lines feel better than pages.
curated-dafont-keshia-gf-noto-serif-hk: Snug, gem-cut letters give Keshia its look. Noto Serif HK backs it up with editorial dignity, generous gaps where curves end, and slightly thinner crossbars, a text serif best enjoyed lightly.
curated-dafont-keshia-space-grotesk: The body text feels crisp and geometric, each glyph a ribbon of constant width, while Keshia keeps faint, gem-snug modulation. Space Grotesk feels more upright beside Keshia's low, quiet script, good for a few lines.
curated-dafont-kg-happy-fs-bespoke-slab: KG Happy writes with stout, uniform strokes and a dominant x-height, cheerful enough for a kids clothing brand, say. Bespoke Slab, a tall-bodied serif, grounds it and prefers brief reading.
curated-dafont-kg-happy-fs-hoover: KG Happy is a handwritten, cheerful face with stout diagonals and narrow, nearly shut lowercase openings. But Hoover's open, refined serif forms are the real draw, better on short lines.
curated-dafont-kingthings-exeter-fs-publ: Traditional and a bit historical, Kingthings Exeter squeezes its letter pairs and cuts its terminals short of the bowl. Public Sans gives it a hefty, trustworthy footing with broad, open counters.
curated-dafont-kingthings-exeter-fs-tabu: Historical in mood, Kingthings Exeter could dress up pull request visuals. Tabular, a monospace with fixed-width, clearly spaced letters, adds a systematic counterweight to that squeezed, middling-contrast heading, meant for quick looks.
curated-dafont-kingthings-petrock-author: Kingthings Petrock is dramatic and medieval, with packed-in letter pairs and diagonals as stout as its uprights. But Author, a refined serif with gentle bowl swell, keeps the mood dignified, though lengthy paragraphs would still feel heavy.
curated-dafont-kingthings-petrock-crimso: Crimson Pro reads refined and bookish, with a faint swell in each stroke and letters packed close. Kingthings Petrock is the dramatic, medieval one, its pen line holding a single width, while Crimson Pro keeps the page moving with its gentle thick-thin rhythm.
curated-dafont-klill-gf-victor-mono: Precise and structured, Victor Mono sits under a Klill heading with big, round lowercase. Try body text a step or two smaller than the heading, since Victor Mono already looks magnified.
curated-dafont-komika-axis-fs-fira-sans: Loud, bulbous and brush-pressed, Komika Axis folds its curves nearly shut (say, for a quirky cafe menu). Fira Sans answers by opening its s wide at both ends, and that closed-versus-open tension is the pair's best trick.
curated-dafont-lacheyard-script-gf-noto-: Understated and sophisticated, Lacheyard Script writes in a cinched calligraphic hand, a good fit for a jewelry brand logo. And Noto Serif JP stays literary and faintly modulated beneath it, though it is better suited to brief copy than long reading.
curated-dafont-lacheyard-script-sora: A calligraphic hand with a steep drop from capital to lowercase, sitting above Sora's smooth geometric curves. Mild thicks against even-weight bowls make the contrast the best thing here.
curated-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-erode: Wide-set and round, friendly as a rolling-ball pen. Over a longer stretch, Erode reads dignified and editorial, with a tall middle band, shallow ascenders and a stroke weight that ebbs and flows (say, for a jewelry maker stamp).
curated-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-hoover: Hoover reads refined and robust, with a generous entry into the e and ascenders held short. Lemon Milk spreads its rounded, single-gauge letters wide and friendly, so the two feel like a loud greeting followed by a sturdy handshake.
curated-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-ranade: Ranade has an organic, slightly swelling stroke and wide-parted ends. Lemon Milk's rolling-ball lines above it are uniform, so a body size a notch under the heading feels natural.
curated-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-martian-mon: Friendly and loud, Lemon Milk could front a pull request visual. Martian Mono's fixed-width, code-style letters follow with generous openings, giving the page one playful voice and one technical one.
curated-dafont-london-gf-victor-mono: Tight, dramatic and heavy-handed, London crams its glyphs close with ascenders barely clearing the x-height. Victor Mono loosens everything underneath, its spacing wide and its strokes without any thick-thin pulse, so the page breathes after the shout.
curated-dafont-loveline-plus-jakarta-san: Plus Jakarta Sans reads crisp and modern, its curves left wide open. Loveline is the graceful one, tucked-in script with tightly clamped terminals, while the sans-serif handles the plain job of being legible, so save Loveline for bigger moments.
curated-dafont-magnum-gf-kadwa: Magnum's e nearly closes into a loop, dense and unswerving. Kadwa, a classic serif with a generous x-height and open-ended curves, loosens the page beneath that heavy heading and gives the eye somewhere to rest.
curated-dafont-maxwell-fs-gambetta: Crisp lines, then a bookish softness. Maxwell keeps every stroke the same width, and Gambetta's gently shifting hairlines add the warmth, which makes this pair good for a handful of lines.
curated-dafont-maxwell-fs-tabular: Tabular lines up its letters like code, each one fenced off by clear gaps. Maxwell above it keeps one constant stroke, so the monospace body and the smooth heading feel like parts of one tidy system.
curated-dafont-mexcellent-fs-supreme: Supreme sets a crisp, open sans against Mexcellent's pinched, retro letters, a mix that could front a nonprofit organization mark. The thick body text keeps things grounded.
curated-dafont-mexcellent-gf-epunda-slab: Retro and chunky, with pinched-shut curves. Mexcellent keeps its stroke ends as wide as the middle, while Epunda Slab, a classic serif with a gaping c and tall rounded lowercase, sprawls open beneath it.
curated-dafont-milkshake-fs-amulya: Casual and friendly, Milkshake crowds its calligraphic letters until they nearly overlap, so it earns its keep when big and short. Amulya stays generous beneath it.
curated-dafont-milkshake-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk reads geometric and unfussy, each glyph a ribbon of constant width. Milkshake adds the casual, close-set calligraphic hand, and that loose-versus-wiry mix is what makes the pair work, better for brief copy.
curated-dafont-nasalization-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans reads clean and professional, with a big x-height and no thick-thin swing. Nasalization floats its friendly letters apart in a short-ascender display, while the plain sans does the steady work of carrying text.
curated-dafont-neon-gf-cascadia-code: Glowing, tall, and uninterrupted, Neon is all one line width. Cascadia Code, a plain sans with a wire-like skeleton and wide gaps between letters, quietly does the explaining while the heading does the shouting.
curated-dafont-neuropol-fs-neco: Neuropol feels digital and futuristic, its closed letters running without any swelling mid-curve, like a single line traced around each shape. Neco, a dignified serif, stays open and gentle, so paragraphs flow.
curated-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-julius-: Neuropolitical pulls its words apart, neon-tube letters glowing with one steady line. Julius Sans One carries extended text lightly, with wide gaps between letters and capitals barely taller than lowercase.
curated-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-lexend-: Lexend Exa reads wide and sturdy, with stubby ascenders beside a large x-height. Neuropolitical lights up its pulled-apart letters like neon tubes, and Lexend Exa can stay small, say on a gaming keyboard print.
curated-dafont-nickainley-fs-chillax: Loose and casual, with curves that stop before closing, this body is no fit for long paragraphs. Chillax lounges beside Nickainley, whose flowing script and long descenders lend a vintage tilt.
curated-dafont-nickname-gf-fira-mono: Fira Mono spaces its glyphs far apart, structured and precise. Nickname adds a cozy, hand-drawn warmth above, though that wide spacing makes a monospace body better for quick lines than extended reading.
curated-dafont-nordic-gf-glegoo: Glegoo reads refined and editorial, its large counters and wide-mouthed curves standing apart from the closed shapes of Nordic. Across paragraphs, that openness keeps the serif text inviting and light.
curated-dafont-nordic-gf-lexend-giga: Powerful and ancient, Nordic spaces its closed letters like far-apart brush dabs (maybe on fitness app workout cards). And Lexend Giga, flat and modern, can stay a little smaller, its generous tracking opening each word.
curated-dafont-nulshock-archivo: Archivo brings editorial ease, its curves opening outward instead of curling in. Beneath Nulshock, with its stretched, rope-like outline, that commanding x-height keeps long stretches of sans text approachable.
curated-dafont-nulshock-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads classic and editorial, with open-ended curves throughout. Nulshock stretches its technical outline above, with an o of equal thickness, while the serif text flows onward, say in a yoga studio logo.
curated-dafont-origami-fs-asap: Unique and contemporary, Origami paints every letter in one constant brush stroke. What stands out is how readable Asap stays, its open arcs and near-capital body height following that poured-lead lowercase without fuss.
curated-dafont-ostrich-sans-fs-hoover: Tall, tight, quietly lavish. Ostrich Sans stands pressed together up top, while Hoover, a text serif, opens its letters wider below, say, for a photo book cover; use Hoover at a modest size.
curated-dafont-over-there-gf-bhutuka-exp: BhuTuka Expanded One reads slowly, with curvy, unclamped letters and a literary, authoritative tone. Over There adds its vintage-military nib-drawn capitals above it, spaced generously, so the page feels like an old field manual with a novel inside.
curated-dafont-ozone-fs-merriweather-san: Geometric and wiry, like bent paperclips. Ozone leads, say, a pricing page, while Merriweather Sans follows beneath with sturdy, tall lowercase letters that make the words look large and easy to take in.
curated-dafont-ozone-gf-ubuntu-sans-mono: Ozone's capitals barely rise above its lowercase. It is a technical display face for headlines, while Ubuntu Sans Mono handles the working text with structured, precise monospace letters and short ascenders over big bowls.
curated-dafont-pixel-operator-work-sans: Terminal-style blocks, retro and digital. Pixel Operator's fixed-width letters sit against Work Sans, whose c tips never creep toward touching, which is a good match for, say, settings toggles.
curated-dafont-plakkaat-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads hefty and trustworthy, its broad open counters giving each word plenty of room. Plakkaat sits above it in closed, heavy, bent-straw capitals, so the page moves from tight and loud to open and plain.
curated-dafont-plakkaat-gf-scope-one: Plakkaat is bold, heavy and nearly closed up, with terminals curling back toward the stem. Scope One, a text serif, spills its counters into open space beneath it, with stubby ascenders next to a big x-height.
curated-dafont-porcelain-gf-fira-code: Fira Code leads with a precise, technical monospace voice and open channels between letters. Porcelain's compressed, razor-thin accents suit a roadmap page, and Fira Code does best at a slightly larger size.
curated-dafont-porky-s-fs-asap: Porky's has a big x-height and an s with jaws nearly clamped shut. Asap answers in readable open arcs, with body height close to its capitals, so retro warmth sits over plain, practical text.
curated-dafont-prime-fs-ranade: Ranade spreads its sans letters out, with stroke ends held well apart. Prime sits tighter above it, its closed shapes and bulky lowercase giving a login and signup form, say, a firm header over a loose, breathing body.
curated-dafont-punkboy-fs-erode: Erode reads like a serif with a soft, tall middle band and gentle weight shifts. Punkboy is best at blunt, tightly packed shouting, while Erode does its finest work as a patient text face, say, for a songwriter lyric sheet.
curated-dafont-punkboy-fs-supreme: Punkboy hits hard, with closed bowls that never thin at the sides. Supreme follows in a dense, heavy-looking strip of plain sans, its letters held open, so a long passage feels crisp and sturdy rather than fussy.
curated-dafont-punkboy-fs-trench-slab: Punkboy stamps out display letters with downstrokes that are never heavier than the rest. Trench Slab then settles into a dignified serif with almost no gap between x-height and caps, made for short stretches of reading.
curated-dafont-punkboy-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum reads tall and open, its serif x-height standing like squared-off woodblock type. Over a longer stretch, that height and the wide-mouthed c keep the lines dignified and easy to follow, while Punkboy stays shut tight above.
curated-dafont-quantum-bitter: Clean and technical, Quantum spaces its letters loosely and keeps every stroke at a uniform thickness. And Bitter, the slab-serif, grounds things with a very large lowercase eye and a gap you can see through in each s.
curated-dafont-quantum-gf-lexend-tera: Quantum has a clean, technical look, with short ascenders and loose letterfit that earns its keep big and brief. Lexend Tera, a sans-serif, runs below it in a single plotter-pen line, say, for a racing game ui.
curated-dafont-quark-fs-merriweather-san: Merriweather Sans reads sturdy and large, its tall lowercase and open-eyed e making words look planted. And Quark brings the thin, even line of a technical drawing pen, so the two feel like a blueprint beside a billboard.
curated-dafont-quark-gf-courier-prime: Quark draws geometric, contrast-free strokes with a spacious c, like a technical pen at work. Courier Prime, the monospace, echoes that drafting-pen steadiness, and that shared precision is the pair's real hook.
curated-dafont-radikal-fs-ranade: Radikal bends its s curves like wire, never thinning at the spine, and earns its keep when set big and short. Ranade loosens up below.
curated-dafont-raustila-fs-bespoke-serif: Bespoke Serif has a dignified text serif voice, its thin strokes half the weight of thick ones, under Raustila's tightly packed calligraphic hand (a letterpress invitation, perhaps). Best enjoyed in modest doses.
curated-dafont-raustila-fs-recia: Expressive Raustila writes with a calligraphic hand, its neighbors nearly touching. Recia follows in a classic serif with generous openings and only a faint modulation, so keep it to brief reading.
curated-dafont-redux-archivo: Wide, geometric and confident, Redux spaces its enlarged lowercase out like an accounting firm wordmark waiting to happen, while Archivo grounds it with open curves and a commanding x-height. Longer text goes down smoothly.
curated-dafont-redux-gf-graduate:
Graduate is a dignified text serif with generous white between its letters.

Over a long stretch it holds a steady, unvarying line, with capitals and lowercase nearly the same height, while Redux above shows a quiet variation inside each letter.
curated-dafont-respective-fs-spline-sans: Respective's pen-written letters send their ascenders well past everything else, dense and understated, and Spline Sans opens up beneath them, say for a yacht charter brand. Closed forms meet open ones.
curated-dafont-respective-gf-red-hat-mon: Respective's ascenders poke up well past its flowing pen-written letters. Make that heading small and Red Hat Mono, a fixed-width monospace with a ballpoint-thin stroke, would pull the focus its way.
curated-dafont-riesling-gf-aref-ruqaa: Heavy stems, hairline serifs, pure vintage. Aref Ruqaa follows as a classic serif with open bowls and a mild, friendly contrast, which welcomes the eye across a longer stretch of text.
curated-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-be-vi: Warm, tightly knit monoline letters, nearly overlapping, say for a fairy tale book cover. Be Vietnam Pro shares that build, its curve endings staying well apart, so the two read as one family.
curated-dafont-rumble-brave-gf-biorhyme:
BioRhyme reads bookish and refined, its curve ends stopping like brush strokes lifted early.

Rumble Brave sits beside it with sturdy thins and tight fit, a nostalgic, diner menu sort of pairing.
curated-dafont-rumble-brave-outfit: Outfit draws every curve like bent cable, finishing well before it closes, a sans with no swelling or thinning. And Rumble Brave, with its sturdy thins, gives a nostalgic yearbook feel to the page.
curated-dafont-rumble-brave-plus-jakarta: Rumble Brave packs its letters shoulder to shoulder, with sturdy hairlines. Plus Jakarta Sans keeps one line weight and holds its curve endings apart, so pages of text go down smoothly, while the heading suits a few lines.
curated-dafont-saddlebag-gf-dm-mono: Rugged and vintage, Saddlebag keeps its hairlines surprisingly sturdy. DM Mono, a monospace with a plotter-pen line, stretches words wide and pulls terminals back, a measured pace that suits short stretches.
curated-dafont-sansumi-fs-merriweather-s: Sansumi draws flat, unmodulated strokes with wide tracking and a modest first capital. Merriweather Sans, plain sans with tall lowercase that makes words look sturdy, carries longer reading on a solid, readable footing.
curated-dafont-satisfaction-fs-amulya: Low-slung lowercase gives Satisfaction a casual lean, maybe for handmade baby gifts. Amulya, a sans-serif with generous curve gaps, lifts the snug script into plain view, and the whole thing wants only a few lines.
curated-dafont-satisfaction-gf-google-sa: Google Sans Code reads with a measured, spaced-out beat. Satisfaction's script is snug and low-slung against fixed-width monospace, a sharp tension that sits well on a jewelry maker stamp, where only light reading is asked.
curated-dafont-scriptina-gf-cutive-mono: Pen-flowing and low as masonry, Scriptina spreads out wide. Cutive Mono, a monospace of typewriter letters with wide terminal gaps, ticks along line by line, though it is built for brief visits.
curated-dafont-selima-fs-neco: Selima writes in tightly snugged, pen-drawn letters with squeezed openings, flowing across the line like quick handwriting. Neco, a serif, stays dignified and open, though quick visits suit it.
curated-dafont-selima-fs-tabular: Tabular, a fixed-width monospace, could sit under a youtube channel logo. Selima handles the flowing, expressive flourish, while Tabular's rope-thin line and clear gaps handle systematic detail in short bursts.
curated-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-roboto-sl: Middle-heavy lines with open throats make the text feel structured and precise. Roboto Slab, a slab-serif, can drop a size or two below SF Wonder Comic, whose dense, tall words carry the punch.
curated-dafont-shlop-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Shlop's oversized lowercase, pinched and tightly packed, drips with horror, an easy fit for a toy brand logo. Pilcrow Rounded's warm, open curves soften it, though only brief text suits.
curated-dafont-starborn-gf-libertinus-mo: Dreamy and spaced way out, Starborn could headline a code snippet image. Libertinus Mono sits underneath in fixed-width, precise lines, its gentle stroke shifts grounding the floaty letters above.
curated-dafont-stencil-fs-gambetta: Gambetta reads bookish and graceful, its strokes swelling gently. Stencil, crowded into a compact line with broad dark verticals and hairline horizontals, hits hard above it, so the pair feels like a shout followed by a thoughtful aside.
curated-dafont-stencil-gf-google-sans-co: Stencil's broad dark verticals and hairline horizontals look cut from both ink and thread. It grabs attention with a compact, forceful line, while Google Sans Code lays out a measured, uniform monospace beat for the detail.
curated-dafont-stencilia-gf-hanuman: Stencilia brings structural, striking letters with spacious gaps at the curve ends. Hanuman, a refined serif with a high-waisted lowercase, carries the reading with a traditional, steady feel over a full page.
curated-dafont-stentiga-gf-nova-mono: Luxurious, widely tracked capitals open Stentiga, with crossbars as heavy as the stems. Nova Mono follows in a technical monospace, drawn like a pen on a blueprint, so the showy top and the exacting text sit apart without clashing.
curated-dafont-tahu-fs-recia: Smooth, tube-like script with a stamped, authoritative look. Recia, a sharp serif whose modest stroke contrast shows up mainly on close inspection, gives it a firm, readable partner underneath.
curated-dafont-teutonic-crimson-pro: Flat, stencil-cut and imposing, Teutonic is all single-weight strokes. Crimson Pro, a refined serif with a soft thick and thin rhythm, would read gracefully over a longer page, though it holds up best when the lines stay few.
curated-dafont-thunderstorm-fs-neco: Neco reads dignified, with strokes that swell measuredly from hairline to stem. Thunderstorm's tall caps and petite lowercase, packed tight like ship planks, crackle above it, and the two make a lively, lopsided partnership.
curated-dafont-tomatoes-outfit: Tomatoes writes in flowing, pen-made letters that sit low on the line. Outfit, a sans-serif with open, cable-like curves, keeps a longer passage light and approachable where the script alone would feel shut in.
curated-dafont-tropical-asian-crimson-pr: Tropical Asian curls its terminals in like a rolled leaf of tin, fun for, say, a vintage postcard greeting. Crimson Pro answers with open, refined letters and a soft thick-thin cadence, a classic serif that gives those tight hairline gaps room to breathe.
curated-dafont-tropical-asian-plus-jakar: Plus Jakarta Sans draws every line in one weight, with curves kept wide apart. Tropical Asian's curled terminals and tightly closed letters bring the playful punch, while the body font stays open and precise underneath.
curated-dafont-true-north-gf-graduate: Stocky, bold, and a bit stubborn. True North's tall middle band and curves that won't close sit above Graduate, a text serif with generous spacing and stems that never vary in thickness.
curated-dafont-upheaval-fs-paquito: Paquito is a confident classic serif with small steps between its caps and lowercase. Upheaval handles the loud, crowded, sturdy statements, while Paquito stays friendlier in modest doses (a solar installer might like that).
curated-dafont-venera-fs-merriweather-sa: Venera scatters its words thin and modern, then hands off to Merriweather Sans, whose tall lowercase looks sturdy (say, on a login and signup form). Paragraphs would read big and open.
curated-dafont-venera-newsreader: Newsreader brings a gently tilted-nib feel, with heavier verticals and open curves that give it a refined, authoritative voice against Venera's light, scattered letters. A longer passage would read smoothly.
curated-dafont-verve-fs-merriweather-san: Approachable and a little brushy, Verve's thick-and-hairline strokes nearly seal their bowls shut, while Merriweather Sans opens its tall lowercase wide (handy for an empty state illustration). Closed against open is the whole story.
curated-dafont-visitor-gf-fira-code: Visitor looks like a vintage screen, with gaping e shapes and short ascenders over big bowls. Fira Code, a monospace, picks up that technical mood but draws its strokes in an even line, keeping the text tidy underneath.
curated-dafont-visitor-switzer: Retro pixel-screen attitude, straight up. Visitor's gaping e and short ascenders could suit a mecha anime title, and Switzer's body can stay modest in size, since its tall waist line and wire-like sans letters hold up.
curated-dafont-vogue-fs-azeret-mono: Azeret Mono reads open and spaced out, a monospace that's fine for a few lines. Vogue swings dramatically from stout beams to hairlines, while the body keeps its low-contrast, precise rhythm.
curated-dafont-walkway-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sturdy, a text serif with open curves. Over a longer stretch its thin lines and slightly heavier strokes settle into a refined rhythm, while Walkway's compact sans headings (maybe for an art fair booth banner) stay brisk.
curated-dafont-wanted-m54-manrope: Frontier charm, maybe for a cabin rental sign, with a vintage streak. Wanted M54 pinches its curves nearly shut and spreads its letters out, while the plain sans Manrope leaves every curve wide open.
curated-dafont-western-gf-cutive-mono: Cutive Mono reads like typewriter text, precise and widely tracked. Western, bookish with gently crowded letters, loses its presence if shrunk small, so let it lead and keep the monospace to a couple of lines.
curated-dafont-western-plus-jakarta-sans: Plus Jakarta Sans reads modern and precise, a marker-like line throughout. Western does its best work with soft, bookish thickness shifts (think western ranch brand), while the plain sans handles a couple of tidy lines.
curated-dafont-whitin-gf-noto-serif-jp: Noto Serif JP is literary and refined, with quiet, modest contrast. Whitin's swollen verticals and hairline-thin strokes would carry, say, an art fair booth banner, but shrunk small they fade, and long paragraphs aren't its job.
curated-dafont-whitin-lora: Lora reads literary and bookish, its curves thinning gently at the edges. Whitin's stark, swollen strokes and hairlines push hard, Lora's welcoming c steadies things, and the heading wants only modest helpings.
curated-dafont-woodgod-general-sans: Tall and vintage, Woodgod has the swagger for, say, a western ranch brand, with lowercase nearly touching the capitals. Woodgod commands attention, while General Sans carries the actual reading.
curated-dafont-woodgod-gf-graduate: Woodgod stands tall, vintage and commanding. It does its best work announcing things with a wide channel into every bowl, while Graduate, a text serif, spaces its letters generously for quieter, dignified lines.
curated-dafont-woodgod-gf-khula: Woodgod's lowercase nearly climbs all the way to capital height. Khula, plain sans with a full brush-pen belly and curves that hold open, moves smoothly paragraph after paragraph.
